messages:
support_lead: Heads-up — enterprise customer on Dedicated reported a sudden p99 latency jump after we flipped them to Aurelia-v2 ~02:15 UTC. Not seeing errors in the app, just long tails and a few auth 401 flakes. Link to metrics: https://redwood.internal/metrics/aur-12345 :chart_with_upwards_trend:

support_lead: Key facts: model swap at 02:05, p50 ~50ms unchanged, p95 ~220ms -> 1.8s, p99 ~530ms -> 4.6s. A handful of requests show repeated retries (client-side) causing billing > expected. Customer says no code change.

eng_oncall_jordan: Can you paste an affected request id and a sample payload? Also did we change tokenizer mapping on this model?

support_lead: request ids: req-8f3a2, req-8f3a8, req-8f3b0. Example payload (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/generate
{ "model": "aurelia-v2", "input": "<long-document 14k tokens>", "max_new_tokens": 512 }
```

ml_infra_sara: I onboarded Aurelia-v2 yesterday; we merged a tokenizer tweak that changes subword merges for CJK handling. It shouldn't affect runtime much but could change token counts/sequence lengths. I'll check tokenization stats for the customer's corpus.

infra_sre_deep: I'll pull tcp captures and check for network retries and LB health at 02:05-02:30. If KV cache misses spike, we can see more GPU work and higher latency.

eng_oncall_jordan: Repro steps I'd like: (1) curl the same payload against canary endpoint, (2) run token count compare vs previous model, (3) fetch trace for req-8f3a2. Use this curl to get raw timings:
```
curl -w "\nhttp_code:%{http_code} time_total:%{time_total} namelookup:%{time_namelookup} connect:%{time_connect} starttransfer:%{time_starttransfer}\n" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '@payload.json' \
  https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate?model=aurelia-v2
```

support_lead: Ran curl against canary for same input — time_total: 4.2s, starttransfer: 3.9s, http_code:200. Against previous model (aurelia-v1): time_total: 0.45s. Token counts: aurelia-v2 tokenized the doc to 16,214 tokens vs 15,980 on v1 (not a huge delta).

ml_infra_sara: 16k -> could push us into different KV cache eviction patterns if batching assumptions change. Did we change kv cache bucket sizing in the runtime?

infra_sre_deep: No config changes to KV cache buckets in infra. But allocation change in runtime last week could interact. eng-runtime did a minor allocator tweak (A-2026-03-10) — tagging runtime team after this message.

product_pm_chen: This is hitting a reserved customer. They care about predictability — if this is a model-onboard regression we should consider rollback policy for Dedicated. Can we short-circuit and pin them back to aurelia-v1?

eng_oncall_jordan: Agreed. Short-term mitigation: pin customer to aurelia-v1 (apply at routing layer) and enable a canary rollout gate for aurelia-v2 until we have fixes. Who can apply the pin?

infra_sre_deep: I can apply a routing override; will do in 5m and post confirmation.

billing_bot: Automated alert: anomalous token billing detected for customer acct-9988 between 02:10-02:40 UTC — +3.7x above baseline. Invoice hold risk: none yet.

support_lead: Thanks — please pin and confirm. Also collect trace for req-8f3a2 and share flamegraph if possible. Jordan, Sara, Deep — pair up for repro.

infra_sre_deep: Routing override applied at 02:42 UTC; customer traffic now pinned to aurelia-v1. Observed immediate p99 drop back to ~0.6s.

eng_oncall_jordan: I pulled full trace for req-8f3a2: majority of time is in model forward (token generation) with spikes on first KV cache misses. Dump excerpt:
```
trace:req-8f3a2
- oauth validation: 12ms
- request queue wait: 8ms
- tokenization: 110ms
- kv cache lookup: 4ms (miss)
- model forward (step 0..512): 3.8s
- response streaming: 120ms
```

ml_infra_sara: I compared token-level distributions: Aurelia-v2 produces more long tokens in this dataset; combined with larger per-token memory footprint due to repositioned embeddings, it increases per-step compute and cache churn. I'll prepare a patch to restore previous tokenizer merge map and run a micro-benchmark.

eng_oncall_jordan: For rollback plan: revert tokenizer merge map for aurelia-v2 and re-run canary. If perf improves, we can try a controlled re-rollout with extra KV caching enabled for long sequences. Also add a pre-onboard check to simulate customer corpuses for token distribution.

product_pm_chen: Action items summarized: 1) infra pinned customer to v1 (done), 2) ml infra to prototype tokenizer rollback + benchmarks, 3) runtime to investigate allocator interaction, 4) billing to advise customer on cost spike and possible credit. Set ETA 24h for initial root-cause.

billing_bot: Created billing incident INC-7890 (low priority) and flagged for manual review.

support_lead: I'll update the customer and offer rollback + temporary credit while we triage. Keep thread updates short. :thumbsup:

eng_oncall_jordan: Will attach bench results and flamegraphs here when ready.

ml_infra_sara: Starting tokenizer rollback test now. Will post numbers in ~2h.

infra_sre_deep: Monitoring infra for any other affected tenants. No other spikes so far.

support_lead: Closing loop for now — pinned and customer notified. Reopen thread when we have repro or patch ready.
